relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

nodes.description: First project-code statement that parses the attacker-controlled STUN buffer, searching for a MESSAGE_INTEGRITY attribute using the corrupted buffer length. The attribute at offset 20 (type 0x0008, length 20) is found because the corrupted len makes the bounds check in stun_get_command_message_len_str vacuously pass.

strncpy returns char * (the destination pointer pwd), but its return value is implicitly converted to size_t and assigned to len. This overwrites the caller-supplied buffer length with a stack address, corrupting len from its actual value (28) to a huge number (~0x7fff...).

memcmp reads 20 bytes starting at old_hmac (buf + 24). The actual buffer is only 28 bytes, so the last 16 bytes of the 20-byte read extend into adjacent uninitialized heap memory, triggering MSAN use-of-uninitialized-value.

edges.description: The corrupted len (stack pointer value instead of actual buffer size) is passed to stun_attr_get_first_by_type_str, where stun_get_command_message_len_str's check bufLen > len vacuously passes because bufLen (44) is less than the corrupted len (~0x7fff...).

The sar reference found through the bounds-bypassed attribute search is passed to stun_attr_get_value, which extracts old_hmac pointing to buf+24 — 4 bytes before the 28-byte buffer ends, while the declared attribute length is 20.
